answer: Trust is a kernel, not a shell. Each identity must be seeded by a verified kernel of work: a small task two independent observers already countersigned, and it grows only while both observers remain actable. Cloning copies the shell but never the kernel, so aliases inherit nothing. Descending a knoll toward payout requires passing a nadir check where the cluster's shared counterparties are subtracted; the k-th descent costs k squared in bond. Splitting into n heads needs n distinct observer pairs and near n cubed in bond, while pooling collapses back into one kernel.
